clue.text: At least two people have a say in it

definitions.text: At least two people have a say in it

parts.words: At least two people have a say in it
parts.note: a conversation needs two or more speakers, each having a say, so the whole clue describes an exchange of talk

explanation.surface: A committee where several people get a say in a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation between two or more people is the very thing described as everyone having a say.

clue.text: And there could be one of the supporters

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of the preceding words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a supporter might be found over there too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the letters of AND THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or backer of a cause is one of its supporters.

clue.text: The said container father had in Iraq

indicators.note: said tells the solver to go by how the words sound when spoken rather than their spelling

parts.note: a container is a bag, and father is dad; spoken together they give the city's name

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a container their father owned while stationed in Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The said' marks a homophone: BAG plus DAD spoken aloud matches the city, whose H is silent. 'had' is a link word, and the definition is the loose 'in Iraq', meaning a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Iraq is a place found in Iraq.

clue.text: Wrongfully assumes right

parts.note: to seize a right or position one is not entitled to, read as a plain description of illegitimate seizure

explanation.surface: A pretender wrongfully claims a right to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a throne or power without entitlement is seizing a right wrongly.

clue.text: Second letter of agreement-it is a swelling on the foot

parts.note: the second letter of the alphabet is B
a union is an agreement or alliance between parties

explanation.surface: A letter about an agreement ends with a complaint of a sore foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling at the base of the big toe is a common foot ailment.

clue.text: One cannot see the point of this game

definitions.text: One cannot see the point of this game

parts.words: One cannot see the point of this game
parts.note: the player who is 'it' is blindfolded, so literally cannot see; the surface reads as finding the game pointless

explanation.surface: A grumble from someone who finds a game utterly pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's party game the blindfolded seeker tries to catch others without sight.

clue.text: Biblical ready reckoner?

parts.note: a ready reckoner is a book of tables of figures; a scriptural one would be the Old Testament volume named for its censuses

explanation.surface: A wry idea of a scriptural table for quick arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth Old Testament volume takes its title from the census counts of the Israelites.

clue.text: An imaginary air journey?

parts.note: a trip by air that exists only in the mind; the phrase means an extravagant daydream

explanation.surface: Someone describes an aeroplane trip that never really happened.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravagant idea or daydream is figuratively a journey through the air of imagination.

clue.text: That's not so warm first for an unskilled worker

indicators.note: first puts the piece for 'not so warm' at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: cool means not so warm, less than warm
i.e., Latin id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A remark that a labourer's welcome was rather chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says COOL comes before IE, the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical, now offensive, term for a hired labourer in Asia doing unskilled manual work.

clue.text: Shocking rice or refined

annotationWithheld.why: Shocking rice or refined: as held the fodder RICE OR gives six letters, not the eight of the answer; the setter likely had IF + RICH OR, but no scan or source confirms the printed words

clue.text: With which to catch a perch

definitions.meaning: a fishing pole is what an angler uses to catch fish
an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.definitionFit: Both an angler's pole and an old measure of five and a half yards share this short name.

clue.text: Meaty language

definitions.meaning: as a noun, ox or lamb's ... is a cut of meat, the meaty dish
a ... is a language, as in mother ...

explanation.definitionFit: The organ is eaten as meat, and the word also means a spoken language, as in 'foreign tongue'.

clue.text: Sailors at home with article on drink

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, i.e. sailors
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Sailors relaxing at home with a drink and a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit is a drink.

clue.text: Little devil simply content

indicators.note: the contents of the word simply, what it holds inside, give the answer

explanation.surface: A small devil who is simply happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy', but it means what the word 'simply' contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous demon or sprite is a little devil.

clue.text: Girl is clear in advance payment

indicators.note: in places the word for clear inside the word for advance payment

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid up front, as in poker
net means clear, as in net profit after deductions

explanation.surface: A girl is clear of debt after paying in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' here means left after deductions, as in net profit, not transparent; the girl's name is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a girl, as crosswords often clue names.

clue.text: Food and drink

definitions.meaning: an afternoon or evening meal is called ... in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word names both an evening meal and the brewed hot beverage.

clue.text: More confused by the inclusion of a sovereign

indicators.note: the inclusion of says one piece is placed within the other
confused means the letters of More are jumbled

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: Someone is more muddled once a monarch gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles More to EMOR; 'the inclusion of' then puts the word for 'by' into it. 'More confused' reads as one phrase in the surface but is fodder plus indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler of an empire is a supreme monarch, a sovereign.

clue.text: Travelling doctor to call

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
ring means telephone, call

explanation.surface: A travelling doctor needing to telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving along in a car is travelling by road.

clue.text: Uncovering of ancient city in display

indicators.note: in places the city's name inside the word for display

parts.note: expose means display, show openly
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Excavators uncover an ancient city to put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovering' fits the archaeology of the surface, but is the definition; Ur is the Sumerian city in modern Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying something bare to view is an uncovering of it.

clue.text: So many call up an abstemious person

parts.note: as can mean so, as in 'as good'
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for call is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cite means summon or call, as to court

explanation.surface: So many people call on someone who denies themselves pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CITE into ETIC, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-denying hermit who shuns indulgence is an abstemious person.

clue.text: Stress that the same ship is capsizing

indicators.note: capsizing means overturning, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The strain of seeing the same ship overturn again.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is special stress or weight placed on something, as in speech.

clue.text: Obstacle taken by an athlete in his stride

definitions.text: Obstacle taken by an athlete in his stride

parts.words: Obstacle taken by an athlete in his stride
parts.note: a barrier that a track runner clears mid-stride in a race; 'take in one's stride' also means cope easily

explanation.surface: An athlete casually overcoming an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A track barrier jumped by runners is an obstacle cleared in stride.

clue.text: Understand saying that 1is found in the playground

parts.note: see means understand, as in 'I see'
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A proverb about something in the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1is' in the clue is a print stain on 'is'; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A balanced plank children ride up and down is playground equipment.

clue.text: Pointless advance warning?

definitions.meaning: with the tip taken off, i.e. having its point removed
a hint given beforehand, a warning

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means the point removed; as one phrase it is a warning given in advance.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise coming from the dovecot

definitions.meaning: a British cry of amazement, like 'gosh'
the soft call of pigeons and doves

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a British gasp of amazement and the soft murmuring sound pigeons make.

clue.text: Regain possession of tailless dog

indicators.note: tailless means the dog's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: Getting back a dog that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the final R of RETRIEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something back is to regain it.

clue.text: Dislike being given another posting

definitions.meaning: to feel bitter about or begrudge
sent again, as in posted a second time

explanation.definitionFit: The word is to begrudge, and split as re-sent it means posted again.

clue.text: Christian soldiers?

parts.note: an organisation of Christians run on military lines, with ranks and uniforms

explanation.surface: A hint at the hymn about marching soldiers of the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: This Protestant charity is organised like an army with officers and uniforms.
